condition4RewriteAudit.defect: The draft places each purported exact cell value in a single-backtick code span while prefixing the embedded status-token backticks with backslashes. Those backslashes are present in the frozen subject but absent from live file 08; backslash escaping is not processed inside a CommonMark code span. Consequently the literal before operand cannot match, and carrying the literal after operand would publish backslashes not present in the intended Markdown cell.

shouldFix.title: The purported exact condition-4 replacement operands are not the live Markdown bytes
shouldFix.finding: Limb C wraps each full Measured-now value in a single-backtick code span and writes the embedded status tokens as \`QUALIFIED\`, \`OPEN\`, and \`HARD-BLOCKED\`. Those backslashes are literal bytes in the frozen draft, are absent from live file 08, and are not treated as escapes inside a CommonMark code span. A literal search for the draft's before operand therefore returns zero matches; the intended unescaped operand returns exactly one.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: The intended old value, projected new value, arithmetic, standing, and surrounding scope are all recoverable and correct. This is a localized exact-edit representation defect, not a flaw in the three-limb decision or the G23 obligation.
shouldFix.impact: The decision promises an exact MF-6 but cannot be applied literally: either the before operand fails to match or an implementer carries backslashes into the new register cell. That defeats byte-exact review of the only existing-cell rewrite.
shouldFix.repair: Restate both full operands with no backslashes, using indented code blocks, fenced blocks, or double-backtick code-span delimiters that can contain the single-backtick status tokens verbatim. Confirm the unescaped before value occurs exactly once in file 08, preserve the already-correct intended after value, then freeze a turn-2 subject.

consentRule: CONSENT only if there are no MUST-FIX or SHOULD-FIX findings.
coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The three-limb G23 decision is substantively sound: all cited identities reproduce; G23 is available; the new row is a valid eight-cell row that names NT-3/NT-5, its owner, and its harness in the same act; required-now projects from 18 to 19; condition 4 correctly remains MET at 19 of 19; D-145 mappings stand; v3 stays candidate-only, so DR-133 remains ineligible and unsatisfied; and no D9 or implementation authority moves. Consent is unavailable because the frozen condition-4 before/after operands contain literal backslashes before embedded backticks. The claimed exact before string does not occur in live file 08. Quote the unescaped bytes unambiguously and redispatch.
